text:
anjali: Heads-up: spotted a flaky failure in the Python SDK sampleapp e2e tests. Repro steps attached.

anjali: Symptoms: sporadic `RuntimeError: Task got Future attached to a different loop` when background tasks use sdk AsyncClient stored as a global on import.

ryan: can you paste the repro minimal?

anjali: yep:
```py
# sampleapp/client.py
from sdk import AsyncClient  # our SDK wrapper
CLIENT = AsyncClient()  # created at module import for convenience
```
```py
# app/startup.py
async def startup():
    # background worker uses global CLIENT
    asyncio.create_task(poller(CLIENT))
```
```
async def poller(client):
    await client.get('/_internal/ping')
```
anjali: When tests import sampleapp before pytest finishes setting up anyio/pytest-asyncio fixtures or when TestClient runs the app in a thread, client internals (httpx) bind transports to a different loop than the one poller runs on.

ted: yep that's a classic loop<->contextvar binding problem. Also contextvars used by our SDK for request-scoped telemetry get copied across loops in odd ways.

ryan: two fixes: 1) never create AsyncClient at import time; create lazily or in startup. 2) create background tasks with `loop = asyncio.get_running_loop(); loop.create_task(...)` so the task attaches to the correct loop.

anjali: implemented lazy-factory in my branch and added helper `get_app_client(app)` that attaches client to `app.state` during startup and closes on shutdown. That fixed the loop errors locally.

ci-bot: FYI failing CI run with logs: https://ci.internal/5623 showing `attached to a different loop` stacktrace from httpcore.

ted: note for SDK design: we should document contextvar behavior. If SDK stores contextvars (e.g., request_id) on the client or in global scope they won't flow between threads/loops reliably. Use contextvars only per-request or provide explicit propagation.

devrel: can we add a typed helper in sdk-python? Something like `LifecycleAsyncClient[T]` with proper typing for `.get/.post` return shapes so users get better mypy support. Also a helper `attach_background_task(app, coro, *, cancel_on_shutdown=True)` would be useful.

ryan: agreed on typing. Proposal: export `AppAsyncClient` from sdk that is a thin wrapper around httpx.AsyncClient but typed with our ResponseModel generics and has `install(app)` that wires startup/shutdown.

anjali: filed a consolidated issue: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-python/issues/512 - description, repro, proposed API, and suggested sampleapp patch. Marked as `sdk:good-first-pr` and `devex:docs-needed`.

ci-bot: rerun queued: https://ci.internal/5623/retry-2

anjali: one extra gotcha I ran into: in tests using pytest-xdist workers the import-time client ends up in the master process and not in worker loop, so every worker sees a client bound to a dead loop. Tests must create clients per-worker. I'll add a note to the sampleapp README.

ted: nice catch. Also add a short snippet to devex docs about the correct test pattern, e.g.:
```py
# conftest.py
import pytest

@pytest.fixture(scope='function')
def app_client(event_loop):
    client = AsyncClient()
    yield client
    event_loop.run_until_complete(client.aclose())
```
ryan: thanks, this will reduce a lot of flakes. I'll pick up the typed helper PR next week unless someone else wants it.

anjali: thanks all, patch and docs PR incoming. :rocket:
